strengths: Training-free conversion is practically valuable and substantially outperforms baselines that catastrophically fail without training (baselines show PPL >20k or NaN; CMoE achieves ~60)
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple dimensions: perplexity on two datasets, six downstream benchmarks, inference speedup, and thorough ablations
Well-motivated methodology: partition into shared/routed experts is intuitive; analytical router construction eliminates expensive training
Rigorous experimental design with multiple model sizes (7B, 8B, 13B) and clear ablations of design choices (fine-tuning data size, load balancing, expert configurations)
Clear presentation with effective figures illustrating the approach; work is reproducible with promised code release
Honest discussion of tradeoffs and limitations, including calibration data dependence and modest speedups at high quality
weaknesses: Key theoretical justification relies on unproven approximations: Hypothesis 3 (Eq. 3) is asserted but only empirically validated; the logic that small h_i implies small products ignores w_down,i magnitudes. Transition from Eq. 12→13 similarly lacks rigor

Analytical router quality not validated: uses representative neurons as proxy without error analysis or comparison to trained routers; no cross-domain generalization study to verify it handles distribution shift

Speedup results are modest and trade-off dependent: only 1.05×-1.12× at 75% activation (needed for near-dense perplexity); 1.5×-1.6× at 25% activation requires noticeable downstream accuracy loss (~76% recovery even after fine-tuning)

Strong calibration data dependence inadequately addressed: Table C.1 shows 2.2× variation in PPL across domains; no principled guidance for practitioners on calibration selection despite this being a practical barrier
Limited architectural scope: only Llama models with SwiGLU tested; generalization to other LLM families, gate mechanisms, or FFN designs unclear, limiting impact

Experimental design issues: (1) downstream tasks use WikiText-2 for both calibration and fine-tuning, risking domain mismatch; (2) load balancing never ablated despite being introduced; (3) Ka=10 chosen empirically without ablation; (4) single-GPU inference only

Baseline comparison concerns: LLaMA-MoE/v2 catastrophic failure raises questions about whether methods are fundamentally limited or suboptimally tuned; no ablation of ATopK vs. other activation metrics
Router construction approximations underexplored: matching sorting indices (Eq. 14-15) proposed without formal proof; no sensitivity analysis to violations of key assumptions

strengths: Novel and practical training-free MoE conversion approach that is significantly faster than continual pre-training methods, completing in <5 minutes on a single GPU
Mathematically principled methodology with balanced assignment formulation for expert grouping and analytical router construction based on explicit minimization
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple models (Llama-2 7B/13B, Llama-3 8B) and evaluation metrics, with actual measured inference latencies and downstream task performance
Substantially outperforms relevant baselines (LLaMA-MoE, LLaMA-MoE-v2) in training-free scenarios, with dramatic improvements in perplexity (62.30 vs >10k at 25% activation)
Solid ablation studies on calibration data size, load balancing mechanisms, and expert configurations; clear presentation with reproducibility commitments
weaknesses: Training-free performance is weak and unusable without fine-tuning (62.30 PPL vs 5.27 dense at 25% activation), undermining the novelty claim—method is really a quick-start for fine-tuning, not practical training-free deployment

Core hypothesis (Eq. 3) and subsequent router approximations (Eqs. 13-18) lack rigorous justification; no error analysis of cumulative approximations or empirical validation of approximation quality against learned alternatives

Significant calibration data dependency inadequately addressed (Table C.1 shows 56.25 vs 116.77 PPL variance); framing as 'training-free' is misleading since careful calibration data selection is critical
Limited model coverage restricted to LLaMA family only; generalization to other architectures (GPT, Mistral, Qwen) and model families unclear, limiting broader impact
Modest end-to-end speedups (1.05-1.6×) in Table 3 given the claimed sparsity; practical utility in real deployment scenarios unclear; missing memory savings analysis

Incomplete baseline comparisons: missing simpler alternatives (random grouping, individual pruning), different training data in dense-small comparison (1.2B vs 299B/3T tokens), and broader lightweight conversion methods

Multiple design choices unjustified (Ka=10 for ATopK without sensitivity analysis; why balanced assignment necessary?; load balancing appears ad-hoc); lack of ablation on shared-to-routed ratio variations

Statistical rigor concerns: no error bars or confidence intervals, appears to be single runs; ambiguous fine-tuning claims ('recovers >76%' unclear); no ablation on number of experts (N) beyond Table 5

strengths: Novel and well-motivated observation: bimodal activation patterns in FFN neurons overlooked by prior work, with clear empirical documentation (Figures 1-2)
Exceptional practical efficiency: ~4.5 minutes conversion time vs weeks/days for baselines, requiring only 4M tokens and 8 calibration examples

Comprehensive experimental validation: consistent improvements across 4 model scales (7B-30B) and diverse benchmarks (zero-shot, knowledge, reasoning, coding); thorough ablations isolating component contributions
Strong empirical results: outperforms LLaMA-MoE-v2, EMoE, and structured pruning across all tested models; 44.02% MMLU on Llama-2 7B with only 2k fine-tuning samples
Rigorous methodology: clear problem formulation, principled reconstruction objective derivation, fair baseline reimplementation with matched data budgets, detailed mathematical appendix
Demonstrated composability: shown orthogonal to neuron-level sparsity (Table 8) and other efficiency methods with practical integration guidance
Good robustness analysis: calibration sensitivity (Table 4), domain invariance verification (84-86% overlap), configuration ablations, and training-free baseline performance (42.5%)
weaknesses: Speedup claims significantly overstated: abstract emphasizes 1.17× but this occurs only in compute-bound scenarios (batch>400, 32k context); memory-bound regime yields just 1.02-1.08× speedup, which is more typical for real deployments. FLOPs reduction (16.6%) doesn't scale to throughput (14.8%)

Weak theoretical justification for core components: sparsity hypothesis (Eq. 12) and reconstruction error approximation (Eq. 23) lack empirical validation; no analysis of approximation tightness or failure modes. Representative neuron proxy (Eq. 7) assumes activation similarity implies contribution similarity without validation

Significant performance gap between training-free (42.5%) and fine-tuned (44.02%) MMLU suggests analytical router is suboptimal; no analysis of where analytical construction fails or how to improve it

Generation variance inadequately addressed: Table 11 shows sparse models benefit 8.3× more from self-consistency than dense models (+4.72pp vs +0.57pp), indicating high routing instability. Self-consistency requires 5× inference cost; no variance analysis or solutions provided

Calibration robustness unclear: tested only on related domains (math/science/code with 84-86% overlap). Robustness to truly out-of-domain calibration unknown. No principled guidance for selecting calibration data when target domain uncertain

Expert configuration selection not principled: Figure 6 shows substantial performance variation across configurations (S3A3E8/S6A6E16/S3A9E16); no method provided to select optimal configuration without task-specific tuning, contradicting efficiency claims

Limited evaluation scope: only English benchmarks, decoder-only transformers, max 30B model size. No multilingual, encoder-decoder, or production-stack (vLLM, TensorRT) evaluation. Unclear scalability beyond tested regime

Incomplete baseline comparisons: ReMoE and Lory (differentiable routing methods from related work) not compared; hierarchical application (Eq. 10) not benchmarked; recent quantization baselines absent
Missing statistical rigor: no error bars, confidence intervals, or multiple runs. Marginal improvements (1-2%) lack significance testing. Single-seed results raise variance concerns
Load balancing mechanism appears ad-hoc (Eq. 9): adaptive bias updates with γ=0.001 lack principled justification and no ablation isolating its contribution despite being essential for results
